title: Wi-Fi: WEP, WPA, WPA2 and WPA3

videos.script: A wired network has a door. Somebody has to get into the building to plug a cable in. A wireless network has no door at all. Every frame goes out in every direction, through the walls and into the street. {{title}} So the encryption is the door. Everybody in range receives the bytes, and the only question is whether they can read them or inject their own. {{range}} The first attempt, WEP, failed so completely that it is now history. Its replacements fixed the cipher and kept one weakness. On a home-style network, everything rests on the passphrase. {{passphrase}} WPA3 removes that weakness from the protocol, and it is the answer for any new installation. {{wpa3}} This lesson goes through the four generations, computes the key a passphrase becomes, and ends with the settings to choose for a clinic's network.
